thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High 5xx rate detected for Ferris Logistics (dedicated pool eu-west-1) — 5xx spike starting ~2026-03-17T05:12:00Z. Pager sent to oncall_sre_lee.

oncall_sre_lee: Ack — I'm on it. Triage started, creating a short timeline.

sre-arnold: Joining. Quick look at logs: increased connection errors to model storage shard euw-3, followed by worker restarts. Could be network / NVMe flakiness.

oncall_sre_lee: Current blast radius: 27% of Ferris requests failing with 5xx, mostly embeddings and batch rerank endpoints. No other customers show elevated 5xx.

cs-raj: Tagging account team — Ferris is on Dedicated Tier 2 (SLA) and has a queued batch job that started at 05:05 UTC. We need customer-impact wording for status page + outbound.

account-ferris-ops-helena: Confirmed — Ferris ops reporting order ingestion delays and downstream queueing. They are actively seeing failed inference calls in their dashboards. Primary impact: order-to-fulfillment path degraded. They want ETA and contact points.

am-katie: I'll join customer comms. Drafting a short notify for their ops inbox — will paste below for review before sending.

support-olivia: Support ticket #FERRIS-812 opened, escalation level set to P1. Adding logs and sample request IDs.

pm-jordan: Can we get a compact status page blurb (1-2 lines) + longer customer-facing email? Keep internal TL;DR for execs too.

eng-runtime-maya: Heads-up — if this is storage NVMe flakiness we may need to rehome a small subset of workers to alternate storage nodes; that requires a quick rollout (5-10 min). Need SRE sign-off.

sre-arnold: Agree. Proposed mitigation plan: 1) Drain and restart affected workers on eu-west-1 pool to force reschedule to healthy storage nodes. 2) If restarts don't reduce errors within 10m, failover traffic to fallback model variant on eu-west-2 (compatible quantized variant). 3) Keep Ferris on dedicated fallback and escalate if SLA breach.

oncall_sre_lee: Starting step 1 now — draining worker group ferris-euw-1-a. Will post progress.

incident-bot: Pager update: engineer oncall_sre_lee acknowledged the page.

oncall_sre_lee: Drain issued at 05:18 UTC. 5xx rate dropping from 27% -> 12% in last 3m. Continuing.

account-ferris-ops-helena: Appreciate the fast action. Ferris ops says error rate is reduced but still seeing async failures on large batches.

oncall_sre_lee: If we get to <=5% within 15m I'll coordinate a targeted notify. If not, proceed to fallback (step 2).

sre-arnold: Restart completed at 05:27 UTC. Observed transient retry storms from client, added short backoff guidance to support ticket. Still seeing sporadic 5xx on heavy batch >512 tokens.

am-katie: Draft customer-facing email (for Ferris ops distribution):

-----BEGIN DRAFT-----
Subject: Ferris Logistics — Service degradation (eu-west-1) — March 17

Hi Helena / Ferris Ops,

We are investigating a service degradation affecting some inference calls for your Dedicated pool in eu-west-1. Symptoms: elevated 5xx responses impacting embeddings and batch rerank requests, observed since ~05:12 UTC.

What we're doing:
- Engineers are draining and restarting affected workers to reschedule onto healthy storage nodes.
- If needed, we'll failover traffic to a compatible fallback model in eu-west-2 to restore throughput.

Immediate customer impact: Some large batch inference jobs may fail or experience retries/latency increases. Smaller interactive calls should be less impacted.

Suggested immediate workarounds:
- If possible, reduce batch sizes to <512 tokens for the next 20 minutes.
- Avoid submitting scheduled bulk jobs until we confirm full recovery.

We will post updates on status.redwood.ai and provide an ETA within 30 minutes. Your account team (katie@redwood.ai) is standing by for direct coordination.

Sincerely,
Redwood Incident Response
-----END DRAFT-----

support-olivia: Looks good. Add an explicit phone escalation line for P1s: +1-555-0102 (AM oncall).

am-katie: Added. Also include the short exec TL;DR for Ferris C-suite: "We detected storage node errors affecting your dedicated pool; we're draining workers, and may failover to a safe fallback if needed. Expect reduced throughput for large batch jobs."

pm-jordan: Status page 1-liner suggestion: "Investigating degraded inference responses for a single dedicated customer in eu-west-1; mitigations in progress."

pm-jordan: Longer status body (for status page) — paste for ops approval:

-----STATUS PAGE DRAFT-----
Incident: Degraded inference responses (eu-west-1) — affecting a dedicated customer
Impact: Some inference requests may return 5xx errors or experience elevated latency. Impact primarily observed on large batch and embeddings workloads for a single dedicated pool.
Current status: Engineers are draining and restarting affected workers; mitigation underway. No broader customer impact detected.
Next update: in 30 minutes or on significant progress.
-----END STATUS-----

account-ferris-ops-helena: That status message is fine. Please include a direct contact line to our AM (katie@redwood.ai) and the incident Slack channel for Ferris ops to reduce duplicate reports.

oncall_sre_lee: Update at 05:35 UTC: 5xx rate now at 6%. Proceeding to monitor for 10m. If still >5% at 05:45 UTC we will trigger fallback to eu-west-2.

incident-bot: Auto-note: oncall_sre_lee assigned incident lead. Escalation timer set: 10m.

sre-arnold: If we escalate, we need to pre-warm fallback model in eu-west-2. Requesting eng-runtime-maya to stand by to coordinate pre-warm.

eng-runtime-maya: Acknowledged — can pre-warm in ~3m once we have sign-off. Will prepare rollback playbook too.

account-ferris-ops-helena: Ferris wants to be notified before any failover that may alter model variant (to verify compatibility). Please confirm before step 2.

am-katie: We'll confirm with Helena before failing over. Our plan: 1) monitor 10m, 2) if >5% call Helena to request permission for failover, 3) if unreachable and SLA imminent, proceed with fallback and notify post-action.

support-olivia: Noted; logging contact attempt steps in ticket.

oncall_sre_lee: 05:45 UTC check — 5xx rate back to baseline (~1.2%). Marking mitigated for now. Keeping the incident open for further postmortem and customer wrap-up.

pm-jordan: Closing checklist for this thread:
- Send the drafted email to Ferris ops (AM to send).
- Post the status page update (ops pm).
- Create incident postmortem stub and link to ticket FERRIS-812 (oncall).

am-katie: I'll send the email now and cc: helena@ferris-logistics.com, ops@ferris-logistics.com. Posting status now.

incident-bot: Update: status page published.

account-ferris-ops-helena: Received the note — thank you. Ferris will hold bulk jobs for one hour and validate. Appreciate the quick response.

noncall_sre_lee: Handoff / next steps: I'll write a short incident stub (timeline, root cause hypothesis: storage node flakiness) and leave the postmortem to arnold + runtime eng to validate. Reassigning to sre-arnold for follow-up.

sre-arnold: Taking postmortem ownership. I'll pull storage SMART logs and worker metrics, and coordinate with eng-runtime-maya for any needed infra changes.

pm-jordan: Internal comms snippet for execs (short): "Mitigated: transient storage node errors caused elevated 5xx for one dedicated customer. We drained/restarted affected workers and error rate returned to baseline. Postmortem in progress."

incident-bot: Incident closed (mitigated) by oncall_sre_lee at 05:52 UTC — moving to follow-up state for postmortem and customer reconciliation.

account-ferris-ops-helena: Thanks team — looking forward to the postmortem and any remediation timelines.

am-katie: I'll follow up with Ferris with the post-incident summary and coordinate any SLA credit conversation if needed.

support-olivia: Ticket FERRIS-812 updated with mitigation timeline and next steps.

pm-jordan: Perfect. Leaving this thread for postmortem comments.

(oncall_sre_lee reaction: :white_check_mark: )
